{{< include _poly-kit.qmd >}}

Afro-Cuban music grew from West African and Spanish traditions, and much of its rhythm keeps the
West African tension between three and two. The key pattern is the **clave**, played on two sticks
(*claves*), which all the other parts line up with.

## Tresillo: three over two

The **tresillo** divides eight pulses 3 + 3 + 2:

<div class="poly" data-layers="x..x..x.;2" data-names="Tresillo;Two beats" data-sounds="wood;kick" data-bpm="70" data-beat="1"></div>

It is not an even polyrhythm (the three notes are not equal), but it is heard as three against the two beats,
and it is everywhere from Cuban son to New Orleans and pop.

## Son clave

Son clave is two bars: a tresillo-like "three side" and a "two side".

`x . . x . . x . | . . x . x . . .`  (3-2)

<div class="poly" data-layers="x..x..x...x.x...;4" data-names="Son clave 3-2;Four beats" data-sounds="wood;kick" data-bpm="80" data-beat="1"></div>

Played starting from the second half it is **2-3 clave**. Which side comes first is fixed by the song, and
the other parts are written to fit it.

## Rumba clave

Rumba clave moves the last note of the three side one pulse later, which pulls harder against the beat:

<div class="poly" data-layers="x..x...x..x.x...;x..x..x...x.x...;4" data-names="Rumba clave;Son clave;Four beats" data-sounds="wood;hi;kick" data-bpm="80" data-beat="2"></div>

Mute one clave at a time to hear the one note that differs.

## 6/8: the bell against four

In Afro-Cuban 6/8 styles (often called *bembé*), the bell plays the same 12-pulse pattern as in the
[West African lesson](poly-west-africa.qmd), and the band moves between feeling four beats and six.

<div class="poly" data-layers="x.x.xx.x.x.x;4;6" data-names="6/8 bell;Four beats;Six (dotted)" data-sounds="bell;kick;wood" data-bpm="60" data-beat="1"></div>

Mute the four, then the six. The bell sits comfortably over both, which is 3 against 2 at the level of beats:
a hemiola.

## Practice

1. Step four beats and clap son clave. Then rumba clave.
2. Step four beats and clap the 6/8 bell.
3. In the [Polyrhythm tool](../tools/polyrhythm.qmd), type your own variation of clave and hear it against four.
